NFIRS holiday-season fire analysis

Scope: all departments (national). Years: 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025. Generated 2026-10-21 14:10. Primary incidents only (EXP_NO = 0); exposure fires excluded. Aid-given records (AID 3, 4, 5) excluded to avoid double counting. Residential = PROP_USE 400–499; structure fire = INC_TYPE 110–118, 120–123.

Summary

H1 — Thanksgiving the top day for residential structure fires: Thanksgiving was the #1 day of Nov–Dec in 5 of 6 years and the #1 day of the whole year in 4 of 6. On average Thanksgiving had 2.06× the typical Nov–Dec day (median rank 1 of 61).
Split by fire type: for confined cooking fires Thanksgiving averaged 3.64× a typical Nov–Dec day; for non-confined (the larger, more damaging fires) it averaged 1.12× (median rank 17). This shows how much of any Thanksgiving peak is driven by small kitchen fires.
H2 — Holiday season elevated: residential structure fires per day were higher in Nov–Dec than Jan–Oct in 5 of 6 years. Busiest month by year: Jan (3×), Feb (1×), Dec (1×), Nov (1×). If January/February rival or beat Nov–Dec, the pattern is a winter (heating) effect rather than a holiday effect — compare the 'excl. holidays' column.
For all fires (including outdoor, vehicle, brush), Nov–Dec was higher than Jan–Oct in 0 of 6 years.

What rises in Nov–Dec? (seasonal lift, pooled across years)

Lift = average per day in Nov–Dec ÷ average per day Jan–Oct. 1.5 means 50% more per day during the holidays. Rare codes are filtered out. 'Extra incidents' is the count above what the Jan–Oct pace would predict.
